title: Neural bioelectric machinery was an evolutionary pivot from navigating morphospace

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Neural bioelectric machinery was an evolutionary pivot from navigating morphospace

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Ion channels, gap junctions and neurotransmitters were originally used to control cell behaviours toward morphogenetic outcomes (navigating anatomical morphospace); their use to drive 3D behaviour via muscle is an evolutionary pivot, exapted with a speed-up from hours to milliseconds and a shift from spatial to temporal (spiking) patterns, and this conservation is why neuroscience tools work throughout the body.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Bioelectricity: the ancient cognitive glue

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The current use of these components to implement behaviors in 3D space by controlling muscle activity represents an evolutionary pivot: their original usage was to navigate anatomical morphospace (Fields et al. 2020) (that is, to control all cell behaviors toward specific morphogenetic outcomes).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Bioelectricity: the ancient cognitive glue”. Scope: Evolution of animal nervous systems from non-neural bioelectric signalling

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public comparative sequence and function data can test temporal precedence and conservation of machinery. They cannot cleanly resolve evolutionary purpose, a single pivot, or the claim that this conservation explains tool transfer throughout the body.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Use phylogenies and functional annotations of ion channels, gap junctions, and neurotransmitter systems to infer whether morphogenetic functions predate neural and muscle functions, then compare spatial developmental and temporal neural signalling dynamics. Earlier non-neural use supports exaptation but not uniquely the proposed navigation framework.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Deep ancestral functions are inferred indirectly.

Components can have multiple simultaneous ancestral roles.

Morphospace navigation is not a standard annotated phenotype.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.42
analysis feasibility: 0.5
operationalizability: 0.55
data existence: 0.72
discriminating power: 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public sequences and divergence times can test whether the named components are older than brains, which is the conservation premise behind the pivot. They cannot show original use in morphospace, nor that neuroscience tools work in the body because of that history. The historical purpose remains an inference beyond the phylogenetic data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Place ion-channel, gap-junction, and neurotransmitter-synthesis genes on a dated tree of animals and ask whether they predate nervous systems, and compare the timescale of non-neural voltage events with synaptic spikes. Earlier origins and a shift from slow spatial patterns to millisecond spikes would support reuse and speed-up; origins only inside nervous systems would count against the historical premise.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The speed comparison is between living physiological regimes, not a recorded evolutionary transition.

An ancient gene family can predate nervous systems without having been used for morphogenesis.
